body:
Found by lane F1 of #665 (comment 5997533145) and confirmed by R501-2 F1 (PR #669 comment 5997910948) on the new bare-metal store. The shipping saved-state writer chooses the sequence the same way.

## Defect

Suppose slot A is valid at SEQ s > 1 and slot B is blank. At boot, A suffers a transient read fault, a media read failure rather than a content refusal. Neither slot is accepted, so the authoritative sequence starts at 0. The next accepted change commits to B at SEQ 1 and verifies. On the next clean boot A reads fine, A's SEQ s beats B's 1, and the committed change is silently lost (SAVED_STATE_FASTCONNECT section 7; D3 section 6.3).

## Required

A slot refused by a read fault leaves authority unknown. The writer retries the read within a bound. Until every slot has been read without a media fault, persistence is refused and the condition is reported. A slot whose bytes read cleanly but fail validation is not authoritative. No generation metadata is ever taken from unvalidated bytes.

## Acceptance

1. Reproduce in the shipping path's tests (the processor writer and the firmware NVM host tests): a transient refusal of A, then a real change, commit and clean reboot. The change must survive, or persistence must have been refused. Run it with both slot orientations and at the sequence boundaries.
2. A planted control that restores the restart-at-zero behaviour must fail.
3. The A/B power-loss guarantees are unchanged.

Relates to #70 and #665 (F1 applies the same rule in the new module).
title: Saved state: a transient boot read fault restarts the generation at 0, so the next verified commit is lost on reboot (shipping writer)
